title: Rate-adaptive slot thresholds and KV eviction plan for sustained QPS spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Design and implement a rate-adaptive microbatch slot-threshold controller plus a proactive KV cache eviction strategy to keep P95/P99 latency and GPU memory within SLO during sustained high QPS bursts.
background: We continue to observe prolonged high-QPS incidents where the current fixed microbatch thresholds and LRU-based KV eviction cause either (a) sudden OOMs when KV + activation memory spike, or (b) overly aggressive request dropping that increases tail latency for high-priority customers. Existing tickets have iterated on admission and headroom estimators but we lack a combined approach that adapts slot quotas based on short-term rate dynamics and predicts KV hotness decay to evict safely before pressure becomes critical.
proposal: Introduce a rate-adaptive slot threshold controller: compute target slots per GPU as a weighted combination of EWMA QPS, short-term peak (5s), and historical max for the shard. Use a configurable safety multiplier and minimum slot floor.
Add a soft-slot leasing mechanism: requests obtain temporary slot leases (TTL ~100-500ms) which allow short bursts without permanent slot allocation; leases are reclaimed if backlog grows.

Replace pure LRU eviction with Hybrid Hotness-Age scoring: score = alpha * recency_score + beta * frequency_score - gamma * predicted_future_reuse. Predicted reuse comes from a lightweight predictor using prefix hash frequency and recent KV hit-streaks.

Implement staged eviction tiers: (1) compressible entries (float16/quantized), (2) cold embeddings/aux tensors, (3) shard-level spill to host (last resort). Each stage has a configurable cost and expected latency penalty.
Throttle low-priority routes early using a token-budgeted soft-queue when predicted headroom < threshold; routes marked "high-priority" bypass until local safe floor reached.

Expose metrics and feature flags: slot_target, slot_leases_in_use, kv_eviction_score_distribution, predicted_reuse_ratio, eviction_stage_counts, fallback_spill_events. Add an alert when eviction stage 3 is used more than 5 times/minute.
Ship as opt-in runtime-1.26 feature flag for a subset of shards, run A/B for 2 weeks before wider rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Controller calculates slot_target and updates every 1s with correct safety floor and multiplier behavior (unit tests + simulation).
KV eviction reduces reactive OOM incidents in the canary cohort by >= 80% compared to baseline under synthetic sustained QPS (loadtest harness).
P95 text-generation latency degradation <= 10% for high-priority routes; P99 improved or unchanged for mixed workloads in canary.
Eviction stage 3 (host spill) is exercised at most 1% of heavy-burst traces in canary and is logged with full trace IDs.
Observability dashboards surfaced and runbook updated with new alert thresholds.
implementation_notes: Controller runs as part of the allocation agent on each shard host; keep it single-threaded and non-blocking. Use recent EWMA QPS (alpha=0.3) and 5s peak window to compute demand.
Slot leases are tracked in an in-memory compact bitmap per GPU; lease reclaim uses cooperative cancellation (lease owner checks lease state before starting heavy ops).
KV hotness predictor uses a 4-bin fingerprinted counter plus last-hit timestamp; model is extremely lightweight (few KB per shard).
Eviction ordering implemented in C++ runtime path for low latency; stages expressed as prioritized lists with async compression and spill fallback.
Integrate feature flag toggles with console and per-customer overrides for Dedicated/Private deployments.
measurement_plan: Load tests: run sustained QPS scenarios with realistic token distributions (short chat, long completion, embeddings) and compare baseline vs controller-enabled shards.
Track metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU memory headroom, KV hit-rate, eviction_stage_count, number of slot leases reclaimed, request rejection rate, and number of OOMs.
Synthetic long-tail trace injection to verify lease TTL and steal behavior under pathological patterns.
Postmortem sample: capture 1-minute flame traces for any eviction-stage-3 events.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit + integration tests in CI; create perf harness PR and bench scripts. (owner: Miguel)
Phase 1: Canary on 2% of hosted shards for non-critical customers with feature flag enabled for 14 days. Monitor metrics in real-time. (owner: Miguel)
Phase 2: Expand to 25% of shards, include some enterprise tenants under monitoring agreement. Run additional loadtests. (owner: SRE)
Phase 3: Full rollout to all runtime-1.26 hosts after signoff and rollback plan validated.
testing_plan: Unit tests for slot controller math, lease lifecycle, and hotness predictor edge cases.
Integration tests that simulate TTL expiry and cooperative reclaim.
Stress tests with up to 3x expected peak QPS and mixed-length generation to validate eviction tiers and fallback latency.
Chaos test: randomly disable core eviction stages to verify safe failure modes.
open_questions: What default safety multiplier should be used for multi-tenant shards where tenant mix varies? (suggestion: 1.15 for hosted, 1.25 for Dedicated)
Do we allow customer-level overrides for eviction aggressiveness in Dedicated contracts? Legal/finance/regulatory implications?
How to tune predicted_future_reuse weights for cold-start scenarios to avoid evicting newly-loaded KV entries?
Should we persist sliding counters for hotness across restarts to avoid losing frequency history? Storage cost vs benefit tradeoff.
updates: 2026-03-02 - Spike: implemented EWMA + peak window simulation harness. Initial simulation shows slot_target smooths bursts and prevents immediate demand oscillation.
2026-03-05 - Design review with SRE and Runtime: agreed on slot-lease TTL range 100-500ms and staged eviction tiers. Action: PRD updated with eviction-stage latency penalties.
2026-03-07 - Prototype: added hotness predictor (4-bin fingerprint counters). Benchmarks show predictor memory overhead ~12KB/shard and KV hit-rate delta +2.3% on synthetic traces.
2026-03-10 - Bench: ran sustained 10-minute 2x baseline QPS test. Baseline triggered 3 OOMs; controller prototype had 0 OOMs, eviction-stage-3 used twice with host-spill latency penalty ~120ms.
2026-03-12 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298 (slot-controller + eviction refactor). Requesting review from @sre-team and @runtime-owners.

2026-03-14 - Risk review: documented worst-case path where predictive evictions may reduce quality for sessions with long prefix reuse. Added a safeguard to avoid evicting entries younger than 2s unless memory pressure high.
Next steps: finalize unit tests, add feature flag integration, schedule canary for 2026-03-18.
